 Kansas State fans got their first on-court look at men’s basketball coach Casey Alexander’s inaugural team Friday evening, as the Wildcats faced off against former conference rival Missouri in an exhibition game at Bramlage Coliseum.
 The Tigers entered the season picked eighth by SEC coaches, and were at the top of the “receiving votes” field in the first AP rankings of the season, unofficially coming into the season as the No. 26 team.
 K-State survived a big Tiger run early in the second half and fought its way to a close 71-67 loss.
 The Wildcats opened the game on a quick 9-0 run on three 3-pointers, but Missouri quickly added eight straight of its own to get back within a point.
 K-State’s 3-point prowess didn’t extend much past that opening spurt, as the Wildcats only hit six more 3s in the game, ending with a 9-of-34 clip from beyond the arc.
 K-State’s lead never eclipsed that early nine-point advantage, but the Wildcats were able to use a strong first-half defensive effort to never trail in the first 20 minutes, heading into the half ahead by five, 32-27.
 The Tigers took their first lead of the night by scoring 13 straight points to open the second half.
 The Wildcats stopped the bleeding with a Jaden Schutt 3-pointer five minutes into the second half.
 Schutt, a fifth-year Virginia Tech transfer, co-led the Wildcats in scoring with 12, along with sophomore Bradley transfer Montana Wheeler, who had 12 off the bench.
 Missouri was able to pull ahead by double digits midway through the second half after an 11-1 run by the Tigers, halted by a 3-pointer from Brandon Rechsteiner.
 The senior Colorado State transfer guard was the third Wildcat to score in double figures, putting up 11 points and grabbing a team-high eight rebounds.
 An 11-2 run by the Wildcats late in the game got them within four, 65-61, with 45 seconds to play.
 A goaltending call on Missouri on a layup by Isaiah Abraham got the Wildcats back within a bucket with 27 seconds to play.
 K-State got a steal on the ensuing Tiger inbounds play, but couldn’t do anything with it, and Mizzou was able to rebound and pass the ball ahead to Kennard Davis, who got a fastbreak layup to put the Tigers back up by four with 13 seconds.
 Abraham quickly laid the ball in with five seconds left to get the Wildcats back within two, but it was too little, too late, as Missouri converted on both of its free throws after the intentional foul to put the game away.
 Here are three takeaways from Friday’s loss: 
 Offensive notes 
 The Wildcats outshot Missouri overall, hitting 39% (24-of-61) shots compared to just 35% (23-of-64) for the Tigers.
 The Wildcats had one more turnover than Missouri (16 to 15) and scored one fewer point off those turnovers (16 to 17). Impressively, the Wildcats outrebounded a taller Tiger team on the defensive glass, and tied the Tigers in points in the paint with 28.
 The bad 
 The one spot that K-State wasn’t able to compete with the Tigers was on the offensive glass.
 Missouri out-rebounded the Wildcats 16 to 9 on offensive boards, which led to the Tigers outscoring K-State 12 to 7 on second-chance points.
 Didn’t have everybody 
 The Wildcats were without Miami transfer forward Timo Malovec, who Alexander said would be a starter for K-State after he returns from injury. 11 different K-State players saw the court, leaving only freshmen Nash Stark and Devin Hutcherson as the only two healthy players who didn’t register any minutes.
 Up next 
 K-State will play one more exhibition versus Nebraska in a neutral-site game in Grand Island, Neb., on Monday at 6:30 p.m. The game will be televised on Big Ten Network+.
 The Wildcats will officially open the season at home versus South Dakota State on Nov. 3.
